operations.comment: ; ROM-only cartridge: physical bank 0 is always CPU $0000-$3fff and
; physical bank 1 is always CPU $4000-$7fff. No bank-switching context is needed.
; Reset and implemented interrupts jump into the common initialization/handlers.
; Unused restart slots contain erased $ff bytes, emitted as fill.
; Conventional slot labels identify addresses, not callable services.
; Joypad interrupt has no service work; normal input polling occurs at VBlank.
; Boot-ROM logo, followed by the original cartridge metadata/checksums.
; The global checksum is stored high byte first; preserve the original header.
; Sixteen-byte original DMG title field, zero padded.
; Unused new-licensee bytes; old-licensee field below supplies $01.
; $00: ROM-only, no MBC.
; $00: 32 KiB, two permanently mapped 16-KiB banks.
; $00: no cartridge RAM; startup nevertheless clears that address window.
; Header checksum of $0134-$014c, preserved rather than recomputed.
; Wait until late VBlank before disabling the LCD, then clear working memory.
; These are the literal historical bounds, not whole-memory clear helpers:
; VRAM $8100-$9fff, RAM $a100-$dfff, HRAM $ff80-$fffe,
; and $fe01-$feff (including unusable space, but excluding OAM byte $fe00).
; B=0 makes each inner pass clear 256 bytes; C counts those passes.
; Install initial display/work buffers and the HRAM DMA routine. The copied
; 12-byte routine runs from $ff80 so OAM DMA need not fetch instructions in ROM.
; Saved interrupt mask initially enables only VBlank. LCDC and scroll shadows
; are committed by the VBlank handler; palettes use the four shades in order.
; Preserve foreground registers. Poll input, start a two-transfer serial
; exchange, upload shadow OAM and any pending VRAM command list, then commit
; display shadows and tick the shared frame counter/completion latch.
; The bank-1 trampoline updates audio once per frame.
; Clear the completion latch and sleep until VBlank sets it. Other interrupt
; wakeups are allowed: the latch, rather than HALT alone, establishes a frame.
; Paired with DisableInterrupts: restore the saved IE mask and enable IME.
; Single saved mask, not a nesting stack; callers must not nest this pair.
; Wait only when a VRAM update is pending, allowing VBlank to consume it.
; Enable the LCD in both the shadow and hardware immediately.
; Queue LCD disable in the shadow, then wait for VBlank to apply it safely.
; Delay A frames, preserving the counter across interrupt work. A=0 wraps
; and waits 256 frames; callers wanting no delay must bypass this entry.
; Delegate the scanline display update, then clear the pending STAT flag.
; First completion saves SB at $ff91 and starts another internal-clock byte.
; Second completion saves SB at $ff92 and derives $ff93 from old/new samples:
; ~(old XOR new) OR new. A bit is clear only for an old=1,new=0 transition.
; MovePaddle consumes the first byte; state transitions test bit 7 of $ff93
; for a falling edge. External accessory/protocol identity (?) is unestablished;
; the observable interface is position plus active-low button edges. See
; ../uncertainties.md U-SERIAL. No accessory identity is needed by this code.
; Prime serial data with $01 and enable the serial interrupt in IE.
; VBlank consumes the queue at $c901 only when $ffa3 is set. Clear the
; byte at C900, first command byte and pending flag after upload.
; Command header: destination high byte, destination low byte, mode/count.
; Unlike ordinary pointers, the destination is big endian. DE advances over
; header and payload; a zero destination high byte terminates the list.
; DE -> command list. Enter here to test the sentinel before decoding.
; A bits 7..6 select literal row, repeated row, literal column, repeated
; column. Bits 5..0 are the transfer count. Row stride is 1, column stride
; is 32 bytes (one tilemap row). A zero count wraps to 256 iterations;
; valid producers must supply a nonzero count. HL -> destination, DE -> data.
; Literal row consumes one payload byte per tile.
; Repeated row consumes one payload byte for the entire run.
; Literal column advances both payload and destination for each tile.
; Repeated column holds the payload pointer until the run is complete.
; Detached inline-argument helper: pop the CALL return address, read a little-
; endian stream pointer, and return after that two-byte inline argument. Stream
; records: destination high/low, flags/height, width, payload. Height is bits
; 4..0; bit 7 selects width*height literal bytes, otherwise one repeated byte
; per rectangle. Rows start 32 bytes apart; destination high $ff ends the stream.
; Zero dimensions wrap to 256. Requires safe VRAM access. No direct caller known.
; Fill BG tilemap $9800-$9bff with tile $ff; alternate entry fills window
; tilemap $9c00-$9fff. Caller must provide safe VRAM access (LCD off).
; Hide all 40 shadow sprites by clearing 160-byte buffer $c800-$c89f.
; Alternate entry: clear the last six shadow sprites ($c888-$c89f).
; LCD-off copy of three 128-tile, 2048-byte 2bpp blocks into VRAM.
; $8000 supplies low sprite IDs; $8800 serves high sprite IDs and negative
; signed BG IDs. $9000 holds positive signed BG tiles.
; Twelve-byte code image installed at HRAM $ff80: upload $c800-$c89f to OAM,
; then wait 40 iterations in HRAM while DMA occupies the bus. DI/EI are the
; original sequence; this routine does not preserve the caller IME state.
; Select directions then buttons, allowing ten reads for each matrix to settle.
; hJoypadHeld is active low: bits 7..4 Down/Up/Left/Right, bits 3..0
; Start/Select/B/A. Deselect both groups after sampling. The eight-bit rotating
; filter suppresses held keys: hJoypadPressed has zero only for new presses,
; while hJoypadPressLatch remembers held state with active-high bits.
; (?) Physical $0426-$0444: 31 unresolved zero bytes. Could be unused data,
; reservation or a dormant NOP sled ending at the RET below. No supported
; reference/access distinguishes these; retain raw bytes, not a code/data claim.
; See ../uncertainties.md U-ZERO-0426 and the phase-1 investigation ledger.
; Detached return stub. It can also terminate a hypothetical NOP sled in the
; preceding ambiguous bytes; no natural caller establishes that interpretation.
; Detached single-bit IE helpers; unlike DisableInterrupts these do not save IE
; or change IME. Shared tail writes A into IE.
; Timer interrupt intentionally performs no work.
; Unsigned B*E -> BC (16 bits). Scan E bits high to low while halving
; the B-derived weight and accumulating selected terms. Preserve AF/HL; E
; shifts to zero. No signed correction or saturation.
; A <- abs(signed8(A-B)); B keeps the wrapped difference. This is not
; unrestricted unsigned distance. Negating $80 still yields $80.
; Unsigned A (0..255) -> C hundreds, B tens, A ones, all unpacked.
; Count repeated subtractions from $ff, then undo the first underflow.
; Unsigned word A:B (high:low) -> unpacked decimal digits in HRAM:
; $ff96 ones, $ff97 tens, $ff98 hundreds, $ff99 thousands, $ff9a ten-thousands.
; Subtract/restore 10000, 1000, 100, 10. Shared scratch bytes are consumed
; by the bank-1 numeric sprite builders. Not packed BCD; clobbers AF/B.
; Add65 modulo256 to hSequenceByte, return updated A. DemoChooseStage and
; RerollBallAngle consume it for varying choices. The odd increment visits all
; byte values; this is deterministic variation, not independent entropy.
; B is destroyed.
; One-time audio/serial setup, then clear initial game/demo state.
; State handlers may themselves wait for several frames; this outer loop
; advances the deterministic sequence byte and waits once more after each return.
; Held Start plus newly pressed Select requests state 1 (title restart).
; Otherwise tail-dispatch the current game state. All masks are active low.
; Tail-dispatch hGameState: the chosen handler returns to CheckSoftReset
; caller/MainFrameLoop, rather than to this JP HL. Table below is closed to
; known state writes; index scaling is byte-sized and not bounds checked.
; Sixteen little-endian CPU pointers in fixed ROM; hGameState indexes words.
; Normal writes select 0..12; slots 13..15 share the return at $022c. There
; is no bounds check: changing the state writer requires updating this table.
; State 0: seed the 16-bit little-endian high score with 200, then restart title.
; State 1: seed title music cycle at 4 so the next title entry wraps to 0.
; State 2: LCD-off title/tilemap/sprite setup; disable scanline scrolling and
; window display. Cycle request suppression over five visits, allowing title
; music on cycle 0. Wait for Start/serial edge or three frame-counter wraps.
; Save modulo-five cycle; preserve comparison flags across request helpers.
; Timeout counts hFrameCounter wraps, so the first interval depends on its
; current phase; do not read this as an exact three-second timer.
; Reset stage/round/bonus counters, score and difficulty, grant four reserve
; balls, select speed parameters and enter state 4. Current ball is separate
; from the reserve count decremented only when a ball is lost.
; Timeout transfers to attract-mode play.
; State 3: suppress new audio requests, choose a nonbonus stage, initialize
; play without reserve balls, and launch automatically. The demo paddle tracks
; ball X minus 11, clamped to the normal playfield. Exit on Start or ten frame
; counter wraps; return to title setup after an extra 32-frame pause.
; Updated sequence masked to five bits selects a table row; bit 7 denotes
; bonus and forces retry. All nonbonus candidates remain reachable.
; Advance scrolling/ball/paddle sprites, then follow the ball horizontally.
; No player paddle input in this loop.
; State 4: initialize a 24-pixel paddle and per-stage flags/counters. The
; stage descriptor is flags plus little-endian layout pointer (three bytes).
; Bit 7 selects bonus; bit 6 enables row scrolling; low six bits select its
; timer pattern. Load layout/UI, initialize scroll state and entrance displays,
; then enter state 5 awaiting launch.
; Set bonus flag and count the bonus round separately from normal rounds.
; Increment normal-round counter, including demo $ff -> 0 wrap.
; A flags/index -> fixed-bank pointer table at $4075 (two-byte entries).
; Copy 20 row timer bytes to $ca14; $ca28 gets corresponding values masked
; to 7 bits, preserving direction bit only in the original timer pattern.
; Copy and split initial row timers, then enable scrolling.
; State 5: move scrolling rows and player paddle; A-new-press or serial
; button edge enters LaunchBall. Ball remains attached until this transition.
; Shared state-5/demo launch entry: clear launch/elapsed fields, initialize
; ball position/velocity and redraw UI; request launch/bonus audio and state 6.
; State 6: bonus timer if applicable, scrolling, ball physics and paddle.
; Start/serial edge pauses only normal stages; bonus stages ignore the pause.
; Physics helpers may change hGameState while this handler is running.
; Display pause sprites, request pause audio, enter state 12.
; State 7: mute tonal audio/animate loss, wait 64 frames. In normal play, no
; reserves selects game-over; otherwise consume one reserve, restore normal
; paddle width and reset scroll-threshold index to 2. Bonus loss completes it.
; State 8 and shared bonus-loss path: normal clear audio/delay or bonus
; results, advance modulo-32 stage index, then choose stage entry or the cycle
; celebration when the index wraps to zero.
; Request normal-clear audio, then wait 144 frames.
; Increment the layout index modulo 32; this differs from visible round count.
; State 9: fade out, disable scanline scrolling and rebuild the display.
; Show cycle-completion presentation, including two 256-frame delays (A=0),
; redraw playfield/scroll state, fade back in and return to stage entry.
; Shared four-step palette fade; preserve caller loop state across delays.
; Four 16-frame palette steps in either direction; bytes encode all four
; two-bit shade mappings, applied together to BG and both sprite palettes.
; Apply one shade mapping to BG and both sprite palettes.
; State 11: loss presentation, LCD-off game-over screen and disabled
; scrolling/window; wait 192 frames then request title restart state 1.
; State 12: wait for new Start/serial edge. No physics or scrolling update.
; On resume restore normal sprites/audio and return to state 6.
; A descriptor index -> clear 840-byte cell/HP planes at $c000/$c400, then
; copy 14-cell rows until $ff. HP comes from brick field 3 low nibble. Set
; total rows and max(rows-20,0) initial vertical scroll. No capacity check.
; Clear both 60x14 (840-byte) cell and HP planes. Current ROM layouts have at
; most 40 rows.
; Render ten tile rows from layout bottom upward, then the pair above a
; nonzero initial vertical scroll. The loop always runs ten times: for grids
; shorter than twenty rows the byte cursor wraps after row zero. Wrapped
; destinations can enter $a000-$bfff; there is no short-layout bounds guard.
; Before loading, render empty logical pairs 58,56,...,0 via the ordinary
; VRAM queue, awaiting each upload.
; Count nonempty IDs with nonzero HP across 840 cells. Solid type 4 does
; not prevent stage completion. Result is stored high byte $ffc8, low $ffc9.
; hBrickRow/Column -> tile selected by two four-pixel cells: occupancy 1/2/3
; selects definition field 0/1/2. Empty is $ff; lower nonzero ID wins. Queue
; at $9821+floor(row/2)*32+column and again 14 tiles right for 112-pixel
; horizontal wrap.
; Build a 28-tile literal row command from 14 paired-cell columns. Repeat the
; first 14 tiles horizontally for wrap, append zero sentinel and mark
; pending.
; Tick twenty row timers at CA28. On expiry use pattern CA14 bit 7 for +/-
; direction, offset CA00 modulo 112, then reload low-seven-bit period. Zero
; pattern never moves.
; Increment SCX offset modulo 112; increasing SCX shifts the displayed row
; left.
; Decrement SCX offset modulo 112; decreasing SCX shifts the displayed row
; right.
; STAT/LYC service schedules four-line bands: LYC=4*next+7. Apply row SCX and
; playfield SCY for first band. After twenty bands restore border SCY/SCX=0
; and schedule LYC=7 for next frame.
; Clear twenty horizontal offsets and display shadows, then compute playfield
; and border SCY.
; Playfield SCY=logical scroll*4. Border SCY=$70 below row 21, else $b0;
; current <=40-row grids initialize at <=20.
; Move visible logical window toward row zero. Recompute raster SCY, discard
; the row below the new twenty-row window, and refresh edge tile pairs on the
; selected parity.
; Clear fourteen IDs at (vertical scroll+20). Decrement completion count only
; for nonzero-HP cells; last counted removal selects state 8. HP bytes may
; remain stale after ID is cleared.
; Cell ID -> definition high-nibble points. Add to 16-bit score, saturating
; at $ffff on carry. ID zero is invalid input.
; Compare little-endian words and copy score only when it exceeds the stored
; high score.
; Score must strictly exceed the current threshold; equality waits. Grant
; up to nine reserve balls, redraw UI, then consume the next threshold.
; Read big-endian threshold into low/high HRAM $ffa6/$ffa7, advance index.
; Integrate 8.8 position, resolve paddle/wall/brick collisions, then write
; ball shadow sprite. Collision/UI helpers can wait for VBlank.
; For descending ball, test paddle overlap at Y=$8d..$94; contact within
; first seven pixels selects rebound angle by half-X offset, last pixel
; reflects X. Then check ceiling/loss, side walls and brick playfield.
; Normal stage first ceiling impact narrows paddle 24 -> 16 pixels and adds
; four to its left X to preserve center. Bonus stages keep width. Reflect Y
; and request impact audio.
; Probe only while ball Y<$88. Clear collision-report count, probe both axes,
; and repeat once if any reflecting collision was reported.
; Probe X using previous Y, then Y using previous X, selecting
; leading/trailing samples by each velocity sign. A first reflection updates
; the saved coordinate used by the other axis.
; Test bottom leading edge then top trailing edge at previous X. Leading hit
; reflects Y; trailing hit jumps to empty return at $0ecd.
; Test top leading edge then bottom trailing edge at previous X. Leading hit
; reflects Y; trailing hit uses the same empty return.
; Test right leading edge then left trailing edge at previous Y. Leading hit
; reflects X; trailing hit aligns X without negating velocity.
; Test left leading edge then right trailing edge at previous Y. Leading hit
; reflects X; trailing hit aligns X without negating velocity.
; Convert OAM sample to logical row using SCY and 4-pixel height; reject
; row>=60/overflow. Add that display row SCX, wrap X modulo 112, divide by
; eight and locate cell/HP. Row-offset lookup assumes relevant cells stay
; inside twenty display bands.
; Nonempty cell first enforces definition minimum speed. Nonzero HP
; decrements in normal play; remaining HP returns A=0. Bonus destroys
; immediately and passes through. Zero HP is solid and reflects without
; reducing completion count.
; Clear ID, add points/high score/extra-ball updates, request brick audio and
; redraw pair. Decrement remaining count; zero selects stage clear.
; Bonus removal reports A=0 with no reflecting count increment, retaining
; trajectory. Normal removal falls through to A=1 collision report.
; Increment current collision count and return A=1.
; Tick ten-impact angle-reroll counter, request category audio and report a
; reflecting collision without removal.
; Snap according to incoming Y sign, negate signed 8.8 Y velocity, then
; update previous Y. Fractional position byte is retained.
; Snap/clamp according to incoming X sign, negate signed 8.8 X velocity, then
; update previous X. Fractional position byte is retained.
; Intent (?) of this empty trailing-Y response is unestablished. It performs
; no position/velocity correction; adjacent helper is not a fallthrough or
; called replacement. See U-COLLISION-TAIL.
; Detached opposite-direction Y snap, without velocity negation. No
; established caller; original relationship to empty trailing-Y return (?)
; remains unproven.
; Opposite-direction X snap for a trailing-edge hit; retain X velocity.
; If integer Y is not four-aligned, Y <- (Y&$fc)-(Y&3)+1. Retain fractional
; byte.
; If integer Y is not four-aligned, Y <- (Y&$fc)+8-(Y&3)-1. Retain fractional
; byte.
; Use integer X bit 2 to add +4 or -4 to X&$f8, then clamp lower limit $10.
; X <- (X&$f8)+8, clamped to upper limit $7c.
; Definition field 4 forces a higher speed tier when nonzero and above
; current tier; reroll angle while preserving quadrant.
; After ten solid impacts reroll angle at the same tier, then reset counter.
; Detached counter: every eighth event advance speed tier and reroll angle.
; No caller establishes these events as frames or a particular gameplay
; action.
; Increment one-based tier; after25 wrap to3. Store and jump to speed-display
; RET stub, not the detached glyph writer. Does not itself reroll angle.
; Save integer previous Y/X; add signed 8.8 velocities to unsigned 8.8
; positions modulo 65536. High/low bytes are stored high first in HRAM, not
; little endian.
; Two-byte twos-complement negate BC; zero remains zero and $8000 remains
; itself. AF clobbered.
; Use tier-1 pointer, then returned sequence &7 to select one of eight
; quarter-circle angle candidates. Load big-endian Y/X magnitudes and
; preserve each old velocity sign independently.
; Eight unsigned direction indexes selected by sequence &7, with repeated
; values weighting directions 6/8/10. Consumers index 19-entry speed tables.
; (?) Same index grammar, but no established consumer selects these eight.
; Could be a dormant alternate choice set; see U-ANGLE-TAIL.
; Clear fractions; select target speed tier 3, or 7 for bonus/<40
; destructible cells. Spawn at Y=$74 and paddle center +/-24. Read tier-1
; direction 9 regardless of target tier; Y is positive, X points inward
; toward paddle. First paddle rebound selects the stored target tier.
; Bonus or fewer than forty remaining destructible cells selects speed field
; 7, not a different initial velocity pointer.
; Paddle center below $48 spawns to its right; otherwise spawn left. Offset
; sign is retained to choose inward X velocity.
; Store spawn position and previous integer coordinates, then read first-tier
; diagonal magnitudes.
; Store sign-adjusted inward X velocity.
; Write sprite 3 at shadow OAM C80C: Y,X,tile5,attributes0. Physical sprite
; fetch uses the $8000 graphics block.
; Move from serial/joypad input, then rebuild three paddle sprite records.
; Serial sample <$f1 supplies clamped sample-$30 position. Otherwise joypad A
; selects 5 pixels/update, B selects 1, neither selects 3; A wins if both
; held. Left wins over Right if both held.
; No Left/Right returns immediately. Clamp left at $0f and right at
; $7f-width.
; Add selected step, clamp to $7f-width.
; Store joypad-derived position.
; Translate sample-$30 and enter shared clamp with upper limit $7f-width.
; A candidate, B upper limit -> clamp at $0f..B and store. Demo and width-
; reset share this entry with their supplied upper bounds.
; Use lower bound $0f.
; Apply caller-supplied upper bound B.
; Shared stored-position return.
; Always select 24-pixel width, subtract four from left X even if already
; normal, and clamp with upper bound $80-width. This bound is one pixel above
; ordinary input bound.
; A half-pixel-overlap index -> normal/narrow impact table. Read current-tier
; magnitude record, always negate Y for upward travel; negate X for left half
; (index<8 normal, <6 narrow). Store velocity, count hit toward vertical
; scroll and request rebound audio.
; Use half-overlap index to choose a 19-record direction within current speed
; tier.
; Left-half index negates X; right half retains positive X.
; Store X, update scroll-hit counter, request rebound sound.
; Decrement hit countdown; expiry advances vertical scroll and falls through
; to reload threshold. Even after vertical offset reaches zero, counters
; still reload.
; Index 0..9 loads ten rebound-hit thresholds and increments index. At
; index>=10 use one hit per step without advancing index further. Launch also
; calls this shared entry.
; Increment index and read threshold byte.
; Store countdown; shared nonexpired-counter and threshold-load tail.
; Write three Y,X,tile,attribute records. Normal 24-pixel paddle: tile0 at
; X+1, tile1 at X+9, flipped tile0 at X+17.
; Sixteen-pixel paddle still uses three overlapping sprites: tile0 at X+1,
; flipped tile0 at X+9 and tile1 at X+5.
; Twenty-five little-endian CPU pointers, indexed by one-based tier minus 1.
; RerollBallAngle and SetPaddleRebound choose a four-byte direction record.
; Each tier has 19 big-endian Y/X unsigned 8.8 magnitudes, quarter-circle
; directions 0..18 (Y rises, X falls). Sign is applied independently by
; consumers. Tier magnitudes rise from 1 to 4 pixels/update in 1/8 steps.
; BallVelocity emits high/low Y then high/low X; DW would reverse each pair.
